scope_check.before: the range arguments of check `{effect}` do not cover the required scope ({reason})
scope_check.after: the scope arguments of the annotated contract for check `{effect}` (requiredUpperBound) do not cover the scope selected by the local Scope rule (knownUpperBound) ({reason})

scope_projection.before: the range arguments of projection `{effect}` do not cover the required scope ({reason})
scope_projection.after: the scope arguments of the annotated contract for projection `{effect}` (requiredUpperBound) do not cover the scope selected by the local Scope rule (knownUpperBound) ({reason})

scope_widen.before: the range arguments of widening `{effect}` do not cover the required scope ({reason})
scope_widen.after: the scope arguments of the annotated contract for widening `{effect}` (requiredUpperBound) do not satisfy scope coverage for the locally selected source (knownUpperBound) and the destination ({reason})

scope_rule.before: the range arguments of this direct call must cover the ranges selected by the local Scope rule
scope_rule.after: the scope arguments of the annotated contract (requiredUpperBound) must cover the scope selected by the local Scope rule for this call (knownUpperBound); for widening, the destination must also cover the source contract

scope_budget.before: the final local Scope analysis Run still exceeds the {budgetScope} {budgetResource} limit; provenance was forgotten while literal patterns remain readable
scope_budget.after: the final pass of local Scope analysis still exceeds the {budgetScope} {budgetResource} limit; provenance was forgotten while literal patterns remain readable

atomic.before: two or more closed surrounding atoms have the same name, but no one atom covers the required scope; coverage by their union is not checked
atomic.after: two or more closed surrounding atoms (requiredUpperBound) have the same name, but no one atom covers the incoming scope (knownUpperBound); coverage by their union is not checked

uncovered.before: no one surrounding atom of the same name covers the required scope
uncovered.after: no one surrounding atom of the same name (requiredUpperBound) covers the incoming scope (knownUpperBound)

unknown.before: the required scope is Top (all targets); only a surrounding Top atom of the same name covers it
unknown.after: the incoming scope (knownUpperBound) is Top (all targets); only a surrounding Top atom of the same name in requiredUpperBound covers it

scopes.before: to keep the surrounding contract, use an entry whose declared scope it covers; to permit a broader scope, explicitly enlarge the surrounding uses annotation to cover the required scope in one atom
scopes.after: to keep the surrounding contract, use a callee or entry whose declared scope is covered by one surrounding atom; to permit a broader scope, explicitly enlarge the surrounding `uses` annotation to cover the incoming scope in one atom

top.before: to keep a bounded contract, use a scoped entry such as `File.readTextIn` after `Scope.checkPathIn`, and annotate the checked result with a scope covered by that contract; to permit all targets, declare the same effect without scope arguments in the surrounding uses annotation
top.after: to keep a bounded contract, use a scoped entry such as `File.readTextIn` after `Scope.checkPathIn`, and annotate the checked result with a scope covered by that contract, or narrow the callee's `uses` annotation; to permit all targets, declare the same effect without scope arguments in the surrounding `uses` annotation

top_write.before: to keep a bounded contract, use a scoped entry such as `File.writeTextIn` after `Scope.checkPathIn`, and annotate the checked result with a scope covered by that contract; to permit all targets, declare the same effect without scope arguments in the surrounding uses annotation
top_write.after: to keep a bounded contract, use a scoped entry such as `File.writeTextIn` after `Scope.checkPathIn`, and annotate the checked result with a scope covered by that contract, or narrow the callee's `uses` annotation; to permit all targets, declare the same effect without scope arguments in the surrounding `uses` annotation

top_endpoint.before: to keep a bounded contract, use `Http.sendIn` after `Http.checkRequestIn`, and annotate the checked result with a scope covered by that contract; to permit all targets, declare the same effect without scope arguments in the surrounding uses annotation
top_endpoint.after: to keep a bounded contract, use `Http.sendIn` after `Http.checkRequestIn`, and annotate the checked result with a scope covered by that contract, or narrow the callee's `uses` annotation; to permit all targets, declare the same effect without scope arguments in the surrounding `uses` annotation

scope_unknown.before: for a nested projection or widening, move the call to the right-hand side of `bind`, then use that name. If the input has only a narrow parameter annotation, one option is to remove its scope arguments; widening a Top input also requires a result without scope arguments. To preserve the narrow contract, forward the value with the same narrow type instead. For a handler clause parameter, `bind` alone does not establish provenance; using Top also requires the protected body to select Top and may require a broader uses annotation
scope_unknown.after: If the call is nested in an expression, move it to the right-hand side of `bind` and use that name. If the value is a parameter or handler clause parameter with only a narrow type annotation, `bind` alone does not establish provenance. To keep the narrow contract, do not project or widen it here: pass it unchanged to a scoped entry that accepts the same narrow type, such as `File.readTextIn`, or widen it in the caller where the checked value is bound and declare the parameter with the wider type. To accept all targets instead, remove the parameter's scope arguments; callers must then widen to the unscoped type with `Scope.widenPathIn` or `Http.widenRequestIn`. Widening a Top input also requires a result without scope arguments. For a handler clause parameter, using Top also requires the protected body to select Top and may require a broader `uses` annotation.

scope_coverage.before: to keep the contract, use check conditions and a result annotation covered by it; for widening, ensure the destination covers the source; to allow a broader scope, enlarge the annotation explicitly
scope_coverage.after: to keep the contract, change the check conditions so that the annotated result scope covers them; for widening, choose a destination that covers the source; to permit a broader scope, explicitly enlarge the annotation

scope_budget_help.before: split this definition into smaller definitions to retain local provenance; alternatively, remove scope arguments from the annotation to allow Top
scope_budget_help.after: split this definition into smaller definitions to retain local provenance (this helps only if the check conditions or checked values are statically known after splitting); alternatively, remove scope arguments from the annotation to allow Top
